body:
Yeah, this is a bug to be fixed although fortunately low priority.

This only happens for atypical classes of Unicode identifiers. Usual Unicode identifiers work fine and real-world code is unlikely to encounter this (unless malicious code). What's unsupported in lib2to3 is a certain class of legacy identifiers and variant forms. The latter is what we're dealing with in this example.

I happen to have the UTF-8 decoding table on my desk, as you do, so I checked and this example is pretty insidious. It's a base `x` letter followed by a ["variation selector"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variant_form_(Unicode)). Variants are for people to be able to choose which *glyph* should be used in rendering the character. It's ambiguous if a glyph variant should be considered a unique identifier since it's rendered with the base glyph if a given font lacks the variant (as is the case here, see example below).
```
# which one is variant-17?
x
x󠄀
```

rename.to: Parse failure on some Unicode identifiers

body:
Another example with no variation selectors, reduced from https://github.com/uber/pyflame/blob/v1.6.7/tests/sleeper_ユニコード.py:
```python
មុ = 1
```
That’s U+1798 KHMER LETTER MO + U+17BB KHMER VOWEL SIGN U.

Part of our team develops physics simulation and they are used to have Unicode characters in the identifiers to better match the literature formulas (in python and c++ code).
We started to use Black in our projects and one problem we faced is having `Q̇_per_meter` ("Cannot parse" error). This is valid python code and have no malicious intent.
I can give a try to replace re module in favor [regex package ](https://pypi.org/project/regex/) which has support for latest unicode standard (unicode 12.1.0)

I doubt the Unicode standard version is the relevant problem, since (1) Python itself has no problem parsing these identifiers, and (2) the identifiers in question are valid in
* `x󠄀`: Unicode 4.0,
* `មុ`: Unicode 3.0,
* `Q̇_per_meter`: Unicode 1.1.

I didn't dive deep into re module, but fact is that java or several other languages has special symbol for any letter `\L` and re module doesn't. Module regex also has that symbol for any letter match. And  I suppose it works different with unicode symbol. I think the problem is related to how re module works with unicode.

issue.title: #455 Fix bug with tricky unicode symbols
issue.body:
add test for the bug
add regex lib which supports unicode 12.1.0 standard
replace re usage in project in favor to regex

body:
@ambv Hey there, given the fairly low priority of this bug I'd like to suggest to revert the change made in #1047 since it added a non-trivial burden on black users by requiring a C compiler for the installation of the newly added dependency "regex". 

The "regex" library author has indicated that they have [no interest in providing whl files for other than Windows and possibly Python 2](https://bitbucket.org/mrabarnett/mrab-regex/issues/343/wheel-for-linux#comment-55179534) at the moment. I'm happy to open a PR to revert it.

issue.title: Look into alternatives to using `regex`

labels.name: S: accepted
labels.description: The changes in this design / enhancement issue have been accepted and can be implemented

issue.body: We're using the `regex` third-party library to avoid a bug around certain Unicode symbols: see #1047 (PR) and #455 (issue). However, this dependency is costly because it's a C library and compiling it is difficult for some users. We should explore rewriting the relevant parts of the parser to not use a regex so we can avoid this dependency.
